title: Platform systems & services: comprehensive playbook, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Samantha Patel
body:
Summary:

This page is the canonical platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference: an operational reference covering systems and services inventory, standard how‑tos (deploy, onboarding, dashboarding), dashboards & alerting conventions, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective and postmortem process guidance, and the 12‑month roadmap for platform systems. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, oncall responders, and engineers integrating services with the platform.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: core platform systems (control plane, routing, metrics, caching, scheduler, observability), dashboards and alerting standards, runbooks for high‑impact incidents, and roadmap priorities.
- Audience: eng‑platform, eng‑sre, eng‑serving‑runtime, and service owners integrating with platform tooling.

Owner and escalation:
- Playbook owner: eng‑platform (Samantha Patel)
- Oncall channel: #eng-platform-oncall (primary)
- Pager: pagers on rotation (see team wiki oncall rota page)
- Escalation order: oncall -> platform tech lead -> platform manager -> CTO (if P0 persists > 60m)

System inventory (current, owners, brief):
- platform-controller — owner: Platform Control Team (engineer: Marco Alvarez). Responsibilities: tenant routing, config sync, rollout orchestration.
- routing-service — owner: Serving Runtime (engineer: Jess Li). Responsibilities: smart routing, model variant fallback, regional policy.
- metrics-collector — owner: Observability (engineer: Jordan Kim). Responsibilities: scrape/ingest metrics, export to long‑term store.
- cache-service (kv cache) — owner: Runtime Cache Team (engineer: Priya Desai). Responsibilities: prefix/KV caching, eviction policies, telemetry.
- job-scheduler — owner: Batch & Jobs (engineer: Liam O'Connor). Responsibilities: batch jobs (compactions, prewarm), maintenance windows.
- auth-gateway — owner: Security & Auth (engineer: Daniel Wu). Responsibilities: JWT validation, RBAC enforcement.
- metrics-pipeline (long term) — owner: Observability. Responsibilities: downsampling, retention, alerting source of truth.

Standard how‑tos (concise recipes):
1) Deploy a small service to platform-controller (canary):
   1.1) Create a deployment manifest under /infra/services/<service-name>.yaml following the service template.
   1.2) Run: 
      ```bash
      make ci-build SERVICE=my-service
      infra-cli deploy --env=staging --manifest=infra/services/my-service.yaml --strategy=canary
      ```
   1.3) Verify: smoke test endpoint, check /dashboards/my-service (p95 latency, error rate).
   1.4) Promote after 30m of green metrics or abort and rollback via infra-cli rollback <deploy-id>.

2) Add a service dashboard (observability standard):
   - Base dashboard template: service_overview.json (location: observability/dashboards/templates).
   - Panels required: 1) Request rate (RPS), 2) P50/P95/P99 latency, 3) 5xx/4xx error rate, 4) CPU/GPU utilization, 5) Queue depth / concurrency, 6) Cache hit rate.
   - Alert targets must be attached to platform alert policies (see Alerts section).

3) Onboard a new team to platform monitoring:
   - Step 1: Schedule onboarding with Observability team.
   - Step 2: Provide service metrics via prometheus exporter; follow the metric naming standard (prefix: redwood.<service>.<metric>).
   - Step 3: Create dashboards and connect to team Slack channel for alerts.

Dashboards & Alerts (standards and thresholds):
- Dashboard naming: eng‑platform/<service-name>/overview and eng‑platform/<service-name>/runtime
- Required dashboard panels: see how‑to above.
- Alerting conventions:
  - Alert severity mapping: P0 (pager) | P1 (channel + email) | P2 (channel) | P3 (ticket)
  - Default alert thresholds (tunable per service owner):
    - API_5xx_error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> P1
    - API_5xx_error_rate > 5% sustained for 3m -> P0
    - P95_latency_increase > 2x baseline for 5m -> P1
    - Request_rate_drop >= 60% vs baseline for 10m -> P1
    - Cache_hit_rate < 30% sustained for 10m -> P2
    - Metrics_ingest_lag > 5m -> P1
    - Node_disk_utilization > 85% -> P1
- Alert destination: primary to #eng-platform-oncall, secondary email to service owner list, P0 fires a pager to rotation.
- Alert runbook links must be attached in the alert message payload (link to relevant runbook on this page).

Runbooks (high‑impact incidents) — keep short actionable steps and rollup links:
1) P0: Control plane degraded (platform-controller unhealthy / unable to schedule):
   - Impact: new deployments blocked, existing routing changes fail, control plane API returns 5xx.
   - Immediate steps:
     1) Acknowledge in #eng-platform-oncall and set incident channel (e.g. #inc/platform-control-<ts>).
     2) Check platform-controller pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-controller; describe failing pods.
     3) Check controller logs: kubectl -n platform logs <pod> --since=15m | grep -i error.
     4) If restart reduces errors and controllers stabilize, scale to N+1: kubectl scale deployment/platform-controller -n platform --replicas=<current+1>.
     5) If persistent error: failover to secondary region by flipping routing-service feature flag (runbook link: routing failover).
     6) Notify SRE lead and Platform Tech Lead; run RCA post‑incident.

2) P0: Serving routing high 5xx rate (routing-service):
   - Immediate steps:
     1) Open incident channel; page the routing-service oncall.
     2) Roll back recent rollout: infra-cli rollback --service=routing-service --to-stable.
     3) Disable smart‑routing fallbacks that introduce incompatible variants (feature flag: routing.smart_fallback=false).
     4) Scale up routing replicas and collect heap/profiler traces if OOM or GC suspected.

3) P1: Metrics ingestion lag / missing metrics:
   - Steps:
     1) Check metrics-collector pods and Kafka/ingest backlog.
     2) If backlog present, increase consumer parallelism (consumer.instances++ via infra-cli) and monitor.
     3) If exporter sidecar is failing on a set of hosts, cordon node and investigate node logs.

4) P1: Job-scheduler backlog (prewarm jobs failing):
   - Steps:
     1) Inspect job-scheduler queue status (admin UI /jobs).
     2) Restart worker pods if stuck; scale up worker pool temporarily.
     3) Identify jobs that failed repeatedly and move to dead-letter queue for manual retry.

Operational procedures and guardrails:
- Canary policy: minimum 10% traffic for 30m with no P1/P0 alerts before full promotion.
- Emergency rollback windows: maintain last 5 successful deployment artifacts accessible via infra-cli.
- Capacity safety: maintain a 20% spare GPU/CPU headroom per cluster for surge traffic.
- Secret handling: all KMS keys rotated quarterly; do not store secrets in plain text in manifests.

Retrospective & postmortem process (incident workflows):
1) Declare incident severity and create incident page template (use incident-template.md).
2) Within 48 hours: publish preliminary incident timeline and mitigation steps.
3) Within 7 days: publish full RCA with action items, owners, and due dates.
4) On closure: retro meeting with stakeholders; track action items in eng‑platform backlog with label incident-<id>.

Platform roadmap (next 12 months, prioritized):
- Q1–Q2 (near term):
  - Observability: move metrics‑pipeline to Kafka+ClickHouse for 90 day retention (owner: Jordan).
  - Cache improvements: adaptive eviction policy A/B experiment (owner: Priya).
  - Dashboards: standardize templates across services and release dashboard generator CLI.
- Q3 (mid term):
  - Smart routing improvements: latency‑aware multi‑variant routing and canary scoring.
  - Dedicated capacity autoscaling policy integration with billing (Dedicated product tie).
- Q4 (longer term):
  - Private deployment toolkit: streamlined onprem packaging and audit automation.
  - Cost optimization: per‑route batching and dynamic quantization suggestions in Redwood Optimize integration.

Team wiki and ownership matrix:
- Eng‑platform subteams and triage owners:
  - Platform Control — owner: Marco Alvarez — oncall rotation: Marco, Nina, Roberto.
  - Observability — owner: Jordan Kim — oncall rotation: Jordan, Mei, Tyler.
  - Runtime Cache — owner: Priya Desai — oncall rotation: Priya, Sam, Elias.
  - Batch & Jobs — owner: Liam O'Connor — oncall rotation: Liam, Kira.
- Useful links: team wiki (eng-platform/team-wiki), oncall rota (eng-platform/oncall-rota-2026), infra repo (git@repo:redwood/infra).

Appendix — SLOs & thresholds (summary table):
| Service | SLO (availability) | Latency target | Error budget | Primary owner |
| platform-controller | 99.95% | API P95 < 200ms | 0.05% monthly | Platform Control Team |
| routing-service | 99.9% | P95 < 120ms | 0.1% monthly | Serving Runtime Team |
| metrics-collector | 99.9% | ingest lag < 1m 90% | 0.1% monthly | Observability Team |
| cache-service | 99.5% | miss rate < 5% | 0.5% monthly | Runtime Cache Team |

Document maintenance:
- This page is reviewed quarterly by eng‑platform leads.
- File JIRA ticket for any corrective actions discovered in retros.

Contacts and resources:
- Slack: #eng-platform, #eng-platform-oncall
- PagerDuty: Redwood Platform rotation (see oncall rota)
